transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been worrying a lot more than I think makes sense. It’s kind of… everything. Work, clients, the market, my family, money. Even whether moving to the condo was the right choice. It just feels bigger than what’s actually going on.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yes… I’d say it is. Even when I tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” it doesn’t really stop. One thing just leads to another, and then I realize I’ve spent half an hour going over some small detail I meant to let go.
For at least the past 6 months, have you been worrying like this more days than not?
Yes. It’s been… more days than not, I think. Probably about a year and a couple months now, since after I sold my house and moved into the condo.
Do you feel this worrying started because of the move to the condo?
I’m not sure it was exactly because of the condo… but it did seem to start after I sold my old house and moved there. It’s been about a year and two months.
Do you feel your anxiety is mainly about the move and selling your house?

Not mainly, no. I mean, that’s one of the things I think about… whether I made the right choice. But it’s more like I worry about everything now—clients, the market, my family, money. It feels bigger than what’s actually going on.
When you’ve been feeling this worried, have you also noticed your muscles feeling tense or tight?

Yes… I think so. By the end of the day my neck and shoulders get pretty tight, like I’ve been holding myself stiff. And sometimes I notice I’m clenching my jaw, usually driving between listings or sitting at my desk.
Has this worry been making it harder for you to function day to day?

Yes… a bit. Work takes me longer than it used to. Even simple contract reviews or negotiations, I keep re-checking things, and sometimes I put off returning calls because I don’t feel like I’ve looked everything over carefully enough.
